title: US charges California man with smuggling $300mn of AI servers to China
key_facts: The US Justice Department said on Thursday 1 Oct 2026 that Greg Lui, 38, of San Gabriel, California, was arrested on Wednesday 30 Sep over an alleged scheme to smuggle more than $300 million of servers with AI chips to China.
Prosecutors say his company, Earthmade Computer, shipped the servers in 2023-2024 without Commerce Department export licences, routing them through Malaysia and Singapore with false paperwork.
The servers contained US-made graphics processors used to build AI; the chip maker was not named.
Lui faces three charges including smuggling and money laundering conspiracy, with up to 50 years in prison if convicted; an indictment is only an allegation.
US attorney Bill Essayli: 'We will aggressively prosecute those who put our national security at risk for profit.'
Reuters also reported the case; Taiwan has separately indicted an Nvidia manager over chips shipped to China.
quote_evidence: Greg Lui, 38, of San Gabriel, also known as Yiu Kong Lui, was arrested on Wednesday, prosecutors said.
Prosecutors say he used his company, Earthmade Computer, to ship the servers without the export licences the US Commerce Department requires.
If convicted, he could face up to 50 years in prison. An indictment is only an allegation, and he is presumed innocent.
why_it_matters_hint: A $300 million case shows the scale of chip smuggling the export controls are meant to stop and the Southeast Asia transit route used.
notes: Event predates the 3 Oct window; TNW published 4 Oct. Official DOJ announcement, also reported by Reuters.
